Solution:
To prove that the given decision problem is NP-hard, we will reduce from the
well-known Hamiltonian Path problem, which is known to be NP-complete.
Problem Statement Given an undirected graph G, determine whether there exists a simple
path in G that visits exactly |V (G)| −17 vertices.
Definitions 1. **Simple Path**: A path that does not repeat any vertices. 2. **Hamil-
tonian Path**: A simple path that visits each vertex exactly once.
Reduction We will show that the Hamiltonian Path problem can be reduced to our
problem in polynomial time, thereby proving that our problem is at least as hard as the
Hamiltonian Path problem.
Proof
1. **Input Transformation**: Given an instance of the Hamiltonian Path problem, i.e.,
a graph G with n vertices, we construct an instance of our problem as follows: - Let G′ be
the same graph G but with 17 additional isolated vertices. Thus, |V (G′)| = n + 17.
2. **Equivalence of Problems**: - **Claim**: G has a Hamiltonian Path if and only if
G′ has a simple path that visits exactly |V (G′)| −17 = n vertices. - **Proof**: - **Forward
Direction**: If G has a Hamiltonian Path, then this path visits all n vertices of G. Since
the additional 17 vertices in G′ are isolated, they cannot be part of any path. Thus, the
same Hamiltonian Path in G is a simple path in G′ visiting exactly n vertices. - **Reverse
Direction**: If G′ has a simple path visiting exactly n vertices, then none of the additional
17 isolated vertices can be on this path (as they have no edges). Therefore, the path must
consist entirely of vertices from G, and it must visit all n vertices of G, meaning it is a
Hamiltonian Path in G.
3. **Polynomial Time Reduction**: - The transformation from G to G′ involves adding
17 isolated vertices, which can be done in O(1) time per vertex, totaling O(17) = O(1) time.
Thus, the reduction is polynomial.
Conclusion Since the Hamiltonian Path problem is NP-complete and we have provided a
polynomial-time reduction from it to our problem, our problem is NP-hard.
The given decision problem is NP-hard.
